gapAnalysis.title: No domain entities — all services operate on DTO response objects
ContentDetailService: 400-line god-method orchestrating 7+ providers
FolderService directly instantiates ChildrenAllReFillerManager (new keyword)
Blocking async calls inside Parallel.ForEach in ProfileService
All domain identifiers are untyped strings — no value objects
No domain events raised for state-changing operations
gapAnalysis.detail:
User follows a profile, adds a review, favorites a file, resolves a content location — none of these raise a domain event. Side effects (e.g., the Disc analytics HTTP POST in LocationService) are fired imperiously via direct provider calls inside the application service, creating tight coupling between the location-resolution flow and analytics infrastructure.

Missing events: ProfileFollowed, ProfileUnfollowed, ItemFollowed, ItemUnfollowed, ReviewSubmitted, FavoriteAdded, FavoriteRemoved, ContentLocationResolved.

gapAnalysis.title: Presentational logic (Ok, IsFolder flags) in domain layer
Typos in public interface names baked into DI registration
gapAnalysis.detail: IProflieService (should be IProfileService) and IFolderServcie (should be IFolderService) are typos registered in DI and referenced in every consuming controller. They indicate the interfaces were never corrected after initial creation and reduce discoverability.

gapAnalysis.title: Large commented-out code blocks in production service files
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentDetailService, UniversalPlayerService, LocationService, and ProfileService all contain multi-line blocks of commented-out code representing old implementations or disabled logic. These obscure the active code path and increase cognitive load; git history preserves the original intent.

gapAnalysis.title: ChildrenAllReFillerManager is an unclassified orchestration utility in the domain layer
gapAnalysis.detail: Core/ReFillers/ChildrenAllReFillerManager directly coordinates calls to ContentProfileServiceProvider, ContentManagerServiceProvider, and BlobStorageServiceProvider. It is not an application service, domain service, or provider — it is infrastructure orchestration living in the domain layer, bypassing the boundary that IContentProfileServiceProvider is meant to enforce.
